mainTopic: Throwing a גט to a woman: what counts as 'closer to her,' how far the rule reaches, and when the גט truly leaves the husband's control
overview: The משנה teaches that if a husband throws a גט to his wife, she is divorced if it lands closer to her, not divorced if it lands closer to him, and in doubt if it is מחצה על מחצה (half and half). רבה and רב יוסף explain that half and half means two groups of witnesses who disagree. רבי יוחנן says 'closer' means who can guard the גט, even 100 אמות away, and a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about a dog supports this. שמואל gives a stricter measure: close enough for her to bend down and take it. In practice, he says, wait until the גט reaches her hand, and a real case required חליצה. רבי יוחנן limits the 'closer' rules to גיטין. קידושין is included only because of a פסוק, and a debt is included only when the lender asked to be paid 'by the rules of גיטין.' רב חסדא teaches that a גט tied by a string the husband can still pull back lacks כריתות. רב יהודה rules that a גט landing on a sloped hand does not divorce her. The גמרא explains that his case is a woman at a riverbank, so it cannot settle רבי אלעזר's question about the airspace of ארבע אמות.

steps.title: The divorce document lies across both people's areas
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a suggested picture of מחצה על מחצה: the גט stretches from his four אמות into her four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and the divorce document stretches out from his four cubits into her four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing a case of "half and half": the גט lies partly in the husband's four-אמות area and partly in the wife's. This answer began before this section, and it sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's four אמות is the space around them that counts as "theirs" for acquiring things. Here the גט is split between the two zones, so it seems we cannot tell whose control it is in. That is why this case would count as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The four-cubit area around a person, which counts as their own space
"Half and half": the משנה's in-between case, which is treated as a doubt

phrases.english: and the bill of divorce extends from his four cubits
into her four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגֵט יוֹצֵא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer to "what is a case of half and half," which began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Half and half means the גט physically lies partly in his four אמות and partly in hers.

steps.title: But the document is still attached to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if part of the גט is still in his area, it is still connected to him. So this should not even be a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still attached to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the picture from Step 1. If part of the גט is still in the husband's area, he has not fully let go of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To divorce, the husband must fully give the גט over to her. If part of it still sits in his four אמות, it is still tied to him, and it is clearly not a divorce. So this cannot be the משנה's doubtful case.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is tied to him": still connected to his control

phrases.english: But isn't it still attached to him!
phrases.notes: "It" is the גט. Part of it is still in his four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case definition given in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that half and half means the גט lies across both four-אמות areas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט still partly in his area is still connected to him. That makes it clearly not a valid divorce, not a doubtful one.

steps.title: Two groups of witnesses who disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that מחצה על מחצה is about witnesses, not distance. One set of witnesses says the גט landed closer to him, and the other set says it landed closer to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as רבה and רב יוסף both say: here we are dealing with two groups of witnesses. One group says it was close to him, and one group says it was close to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier picture and gives a new one. The "half and half" is a split between two groups of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier explanation is being replaced. Now "half and half" does not describe where the גט physically lies. It describes the evidence: equal testimony on each side. Since we cannot know which group is right, the divorce is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather": replaces a rejected explanation with a new one
"Both of them": the two rabbis agree
"We are dealing with": defines the case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture the גט landing exactly in the middle. In this explanation, "half and half" means the testimony is split evenly, not the distance.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba and Rav Yosef
who both say:
Here we are dealing with two groups of witnesses
one says it was close to him,
and one says it was close to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 by replacing the explanation from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: from physical position to conflicting testimony.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Half and half meant the גט physically lay in both people's areas.
steps.terutzMaskana: Half and half means two groups of witnesses contradict each other about where it landed.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה and רב יוסף, the משנה's doubt comes from witnesses who disagree, not from where the גט lies.

steps.title: "Closer" means truly closer, even far away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that "closer to her" and "closer to him" mean actually closer, even if the גט is 100 אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: we learned "close to her," even 100 cubits away; and we learned "close to him," even 100 cubits away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his own reading of the משנה's words. "Closer" is not limited to someone's four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the reading that ties "closer" to a person's four-אמות area, רבי יוחנן reads it plainly. Whoever the גט is nearer to counts, even at a large distance like 100 אמות. This raises a new problem: what then is "half and half"? The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred cubits: a large distance

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
We learned "close to her"
even one hundred cubits away;
and we learned "close to him"
even one hundred cubits away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a separate approach to the משנה's terms, different from the four-אמות approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Closer to her" or "closer to him" means actually closer, even if the גט is 100 אמות away.

steps.title: What then is "half and half"?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the גמרא asks what the in-between case of מחצה על מחצה would look like.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of "half and half"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יוחנן's view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "closer" just means nearer to one person, it is hard to picture a real middle case. It would be very rare for the גט to land at exactly the same distance from both. So the גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן defines it.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the case?": asks for a concrete picture

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of "half and half"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of half and half within רבי יוחנן's approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of half and half according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: It depends on who can guard the document
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן personally explained it to him. If only he can guard the גט, it counts as close to him. If only she can, it counts as close to her. If both can, or neither can, it is half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן explained it to me himself. If he can guard it and she cannot, that is "close to him." If she can guard it and he cannot, that is "close to her." If both can guard it, or neither can, that is "half and half."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רבי יוחנן's own definition, which he explained personally to רב שמן בר אבא. "Closer" is measured by who is able to guard the גט, not by exact distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is about control: who could actually protect the גט where it landed. When only one person can guard it, it belongs to that side. When the ability is equal (both or neither), we cannot decide, and that is the doubtful case.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, "closer" means who can guard the גט. If only one of them can, it goes to that side. If both or neither can, it is מחצה על מחצה, a doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the משנה's test from measuring distance to asking who has real control over the גט. That fits the idea that a divorce depends on the גט reaching her control.

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said,
It was explained to me personally
by Rabbi Yochanan himself:
If he can guard it
and she cannot guard it,
this is "close to him";
if she can guard it
and he cannot guard it,
this is "close to her";
if both of them can guard it,
or both of them cannot,
this is "half and half."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא, לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לַהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Closeness is measured by who can guard the גט. If both can or neither can, it is half and half.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן hears his explanation from Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The "who can guard it" explanation is reported before רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי יונתן. רבי יוחנן is impressed that the Babylonian scholars explain it the same way he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said this explanation in front of רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי יונתן. רבי יוחנן said: Our Babylonian friends know how to explain it with this very reasoning!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone repeats the "guarding" explanation from step 6 in front of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יונתן. רבי יוחנן is delighted that the scholars in בבל reached the same idea he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. The step shows that this definition of "closer" was accepted in both ארץ ישראל and בבל, so it carries extra weight.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Rabbi Yochanan
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan, this way,
phrases.notes: "This way" points back to the explanation in step 6: whoever can guard the גט counts as closer.

phrases.english: He said: Our Babylonian friends know
how to explain it with this reasoning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the explanation from step 6 was shared by the Babylonian scholars too
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The "who can guard it" definition of closeness is agreed upon by רבי יוחנן and the Babylonian scholars.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about a dog taking the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if the גט is closer to her and a dog comes and takes it, she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says: Any גט that is closer to her than to him, and a dog came and took it, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the "guarding" explanation. The גמרא is setting this up: the strange wording will be questioned in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the ברייתא is surprising. If the גט was already closer to her, the divorce should have worked, so why would a dog taking it afterward matter? The next steps use this problem to show the ברייתא must be about who can guard the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (bringing support)
Closer to her than to him

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Any [גט] that is closer to her than to him,
and a dog came and took it,
she is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up the guarding explanation
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's explanation that "closer" depends on who can guard the גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר about a dog taking the גט

steps.title: Why would a dog undo the divorce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how she can be not divorced if the גט was already closer to her. Must she keep guarding it forever?
steps.simpleTranslation: She is not divorced?! Must she keep guarding it and go on guarding it forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the ברייתא. Once the גט was closer to her, she should already be divorced, so a dog taking it later should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the divorce worked the moment the גט landed near her, losing the גט afterward cannot cancel it. Otherwise she would have to guard her גט endlessly to stay divorced, which makes no sense.

phrases.english: She is not divorced?!
Must she keep guarding it on and on?
phrases.notes: He means: once she is divorced, does she have to keep watching the גט forever so the divorce won't fall apart?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת?! כֹּל הָיכִי תִּינְטְרֵיהּ וְתֵיזִיל?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of רבי אליעזר's ruling that she is not divorced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorce that already took effect cannot be undone because a dog later took the גט.

steps.title: The ברייתא is really about who can guard the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the dog is only an imagined test. If he could protect the גט from a dog and she could not, she is not divorced. This proves רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what he is saying: Any גט that is closer to her than to him, but if a dog were to come and take it, he would be able to guard it and she would not be able to guard it, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dog did not really take the גט. The ברייתא means: picture a dog coming. If only he could protect the גט, she is not divorced, even though it is closer to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading removes the problem from step 9, because the divorce never took effect in the first place. It also proves רבי יוחנן's rule: closeness is measured by who can guard the גט, not by distance alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this what he means? (rereading a source)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר supports רבי יוחנן: the person who can guard the גט is the one it is "close" to, even if it is physically nearer to the other person.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what he is saying:
Any [גט] that is closer to her than to him;
and if a dog were to come and take it,
and he would be able to guard it
and she would not be able to guard it,
she is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9 by rereading the ברייתא, which completes the proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the dog is a hypothetical test of who can guard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A real dog took the גט after it already landed near her, which made the ruling confusing
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog is imagined. If only he could protect the גט, it counts as his, so she is not divorced.

steps.title: שמואל: close enough to bend down and take it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה that "closer to her" means close enough for her to bend down and pick it up. In practice, do not rely on the divorce until the גט reaches her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, "closer to her" means close enough that she can bend down and take it. But you should not act on this in a real case until the גט reaches her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his own definition of "closer to her": the גט must be close enough that she could bend down and pick it up. He then tells רב יהודה not to allow a real divorce based on this until the גט is actually in her hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different and much stricter measure than רבי יוחנן's, who counted the גט as close even 100 אמות away if only she could guard it. On top of that, שמואל adds a practical caution: a judge should only rely on the divorce once the גט reaches her hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp one (a nickname for רב יהודה)
Do not act on it in a real case

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן measures "close" by who can guard the גט. שמואל measures it by whether she can bend down and pick it up. In practice, שמואל says to wait until the גט reaches her hand.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two definitions. שמואל's "bend down and take it" is not the same as רבי יוחנן's "who can guard it."
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical bottom line for a thrown גט: be strict and do not rely on it until it is actually in her hand.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא,
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda: Sharp one,
phrases.notes: שִׁינָּנָא is a friendly nickname that שמואל used for רב יהודה.

phrases.english: [closer means] so that she can bend down and take it.
phrases.notes: שמואל is explaining what "closer to her" in the משנה means.

phrases.english: And you should not act on it in a real case,
until the גט reaches her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, stricter definition of "closer to her" than רבי יוחנן's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Closer to her" means close enough to bend down and take it, and in practice one waits until the גט reaches her hand.

steps.title: A real case where the woman needed חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells רב אשי about a real case. The גט was closer to the woman but never reached her hand, and the בית דין still required her to do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: This exact thing once happened, and they made her do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי reports a real-life case. It shows that in practice, a גט that was only 'closer to her' was not fully trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous step, שמואל said not to rely on the divorce until the גט reaches her hand. Here a בית דין acted that way. They treated her as possibly still married, so when her husband died she needed חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A real incident, an actual case
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from marrying her husband's brother

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the practical הלכה follows the strict approach: a גט that is only 'closer to her' is treated as a doubtful divorce.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
There was an incident like this,
phrases.notes: He means the case we just discussed: the גט was closer to her, but it never reached her hand.

phrases.english: and they required her to do chalitza.
phrases.notes: The divorce was in doubt, so she was treated as maybe still married when her husband died without children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that matches שמואל's practical caution
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט that only landed closer to her is a doubtful divorce, so she needed חליצה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the 'closer' rule to divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the same rules apply to קידושין. רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, says the 'closer' rules were said only for a גט and not for anything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the same is true for betrothal.' רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: These rules were said only for divorce documents, not for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It brings רבי יוחנן's statement that the 'closer to him or her' rule belongs only to גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned the 'closer' rule for a thrown גט. רבי יוחנן says not to stretch this rule to other areas of הלכה. This sets up a challenge, because the משנה itself mentions קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: "And the same applies to betrothal."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They said this for divorce documents,
and not for any other matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְגִיטִּין אָמְרוּ, וְלֹא לְדָבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'closer to him or her' rule applies only to גיטין.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה itself includes betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רבי אסי. The משנה clearly says the same rules apply to קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא challenged רבי אסי: But the משנה says, 'And the same is true for betrothal'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רבי יוחנן's statement using the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the rule is only for גיטין. But the משנה openly applies it to קידושין too. So how can he say 'not for any other matter'?

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba challenged Rabbi Asi:
"And the same applies to betrothal"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's limit
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the rule is only for גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly extends the rule to קידושין, so it is not limited to divorce.

steps.title: Answer: a פסוק links betrothal to divorce
steps.stepSummary: Betrothal is a special case. The Torah connects 'and she leaves' (divorce) with 'and she becomes' (a new marriage), so the rules of divorce carry over to קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Betrothal is different, because the פסוק says 'and she leaves… and she becomes,' which connects betrothal to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. קידושין is an exception because a פסוק ties it to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts leaving the first marriage right next to becoming another man's wife. That link lets us learn קידושין from גיטין. Other areas of הלכה have no such link, so רבי יוחנן's rule still stands for them.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because it is written "and she leaves" and "and she becomes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Including קידושין proves the rule applies everywhere
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין is learned from גיטין only because of a special פסוק; other matters are not included

steps.title: Challenge: the same rule is used for paying a debt
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: a teaching applies the 'closer' rule to a debt payment that is thrown. If it is closer to the lender, the debt is paid. If it is closer to the borrower, he still owes. If it is half and half, they split the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another challenge: 'And the same is true for a debt. If the lender said, "Throw me my payment," and the borrower threw it: if it landed closer to the lender, the borrower is cleared. If it landed closer to the borrower, he still owes. If it is half and half, they split it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן again, this time from money matters. The next step begins the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching uses the 'closer' rule for a debt, which is not marriage or divorce. There is no פסוק like 'and she leaves… and she becomes' to explain it. So the question is back: the rule seems to apply beyond גיטין.

phrases.english: He challenged him: "And the same applies to a debt:
if the lender said 'Throw me my debt' and he threw it to him,
if it landed closer to the lender, the borrower is cleared;
if it landed closer to the borrower, the borrower is still obligated;
if it is half and half, the two of them split it!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יוחנן after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the rule is only for גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching applies the 'closer' rule to debts, and the פסוק that explained קידושין does not cover money matters.

steps.title: The lender told the borrower to throw the payment
steps.stepSummary: The debt case follows the 'closer' rules only because the lender said, 'Throw it to me and you are free.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a case where the lender said to the borrower: 'Throw my money to me, and you will be free of the debt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן against the debt challenge. It says the debt case is a special situation where the lender himself asked for the money to be thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the 'closer' rules apply only to a גט. Normally they would not apply to a debt payment. Here they do because the lender agreed to receive the money by throwing, so the rule comes from his own words, not from the general law of debts.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrow case to answer a challenge)
My debt (the money owed to me)
And you will be free (of the obligation)

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where he said to him:
phrases.notes: The lender is speaking to the borrower.

phrases.english: "Throw my debt to me, and you will be free."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the debt challenge of Step 16 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a stipulation by the lender
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The debt teaching seemed to apply the 'closer' rules to ordinary debts, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only applies because the lender himself told the borrower to throw the money.

steps.title: If so, why teach it at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the lender made a clear agreement, the result seems obvious, so why state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If the lender set up the deal himself, there seems to be nothing new to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the lender agreed, it is obvious he must accept his own terms. So a teaching built on such an agreement seems to tell us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (Why is this needed? It is obvious!)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17 as making the teaching obvious.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that only repeats what the lender agreed to is obvious and should not need to be taught.

steps.title: He said to throw it by the rules of divorce
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is needed where the lender said, 'Throw it to me by the rules of גיטין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he said: 'Throw my debt to me the way a גט is given.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the case. The lender did not just say 'throw it.' He said to follow the rules of גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'closer' rules (closer to the lender, closer to the borrower, half and half) apply because the lender borrowed them from גיטין by his own words. This is where the full set of 'closer' rules comes from in a money case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this specific case)
By the rules of bills of divorce

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he said to him:
"Throw my debt to me by the rules of bills of divorce."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by making the case more specific.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lender only said 'throw it', which seems too obvious to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said to follow the rules of גיטין, which brings in the full 'closer' system.

steps.title: Still, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: Even with 'by the rules of גיטין', he clearly agreed, so it still seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question again. Even this clearer agreement seems too obvious to need a teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'by the rules of גיטין' is even more clear-cut. That makes the teaching look even more obvious.

phrases.english: And still, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the 'obvious' challenge against the sharper case of Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit agreement to use the rules of גיטין obviously binds him, so there is nothing to teach.

steps.title: He cannot say 'I was joking'
steps.stepSummary: The teaching tells us the lender cannot back out by claiming he was only teasing.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought he could say, 'I was only joking with you.' So the teaching tells us he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point of the teaching. The lender is held to his odd agreement and cannot later call it a joke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling someone to pay a debt 'like a גט' sounds strange, so one might think it was not meant seriously. The teaching shows that his words are binding. This ends the defense of רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן still stands: the 'closer' rules belong to גט (and קידושין). They apply to a debt only when the lender himself agreed to the rules of גיטין, and he cannot take that back by saying he was joking.

phrases.english: You might have said
he can say to him:
"I am joking with you";
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by showing the new point of the teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what is new in the teaching (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lender could cancel his strange agreement by saying he was joking.
steps.terutzMaskana: His agreement holds, and the 'closer' rules decide the payment.

steps.title: A גט in her hand with a string in his hand
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא: if the husband can still pull the גט back by the string, she is not divorced. If he cannot, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The גט is in her hand, and a string tied to it is in his hand. If he can pull it away and bring it back to himself, she is not divorced. If he cannot, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רב חסדא about a husband who still holds a string tied to the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding the גט in her hand is usually enough to divorce her. But if the husband can still pull it back, the גט is not fully out of his control. The deciding question is whether he can actually take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: To pull it away (out of her hand)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The bill of divorce is in her hand and a string is in his hand;
phrases.notes: The string is tied to the גט, so the husband is still connected to it.

phrases.english: if he can pull it away and bring it to himself,
she is not divorced;
and if not, she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about giving the גט, separate from the debt discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband can pull the גט back by a string he holds, she is not divorced. If he cannot, she is divorced.

steps.title: The reason: a divorce needs a full cut-off
steps.stepSummary: She is not divorced because a divorce needs כריתות, a complete cutting off, and that is missing here.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? We need a complete cut-off, and there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא's ruling is so, and answers in one line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls a גט a 'ספר כריתות', a document of cutting off. If the husband can still pull the גט back, he has not fully let it go, so the bond between them is not cut.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete cutting off (between husband and wife)

steps.whatToRemember: A גט works only when the husband fully lets go. If he can still pull it back, it lacks כריתות and she is not divorced.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
We require a cutting off, and there is none.
phrases.notes: This comes from the Torah calling a גט 'ספר כריתות' (דברים 24:1).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב חסדא's ruling in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why she is not divorced when the husband can pull the גט back
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A divorce needs כריתות, a full cut-off, and it is missing while he can still pull the גט back.

steps.title: A גט landing on a sloped hand does not divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה: if her hand was tilted like a slope and the גט was thrown onto it, she is not divorced, even though it reached her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If her hand was shaped like a slope and he threw the גט to her, she is not divorced, even though the גט reached her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling about a thrown גט that touches the woman's hand but cannot stay there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching her hand is not enough. Her hand only acquires the גט if it can actually hold it. A sloped hand lets the גט slide right off, so she never really received it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If her hand was shaped like a slope,
and he threw it to her;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ גֵּט לְיָדָהּ –
phrases.english: even though the bill of divorce reached her hand
she is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same topic of throwing a גט, following רב חסדא's string case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט that lands on a sloped hand it cannot rest on does not divorce her.

steps.title: But it falls into her four אמות
steps.stepSummary: Why is she not divorced? When the גט slides off her hand, it lands within her ארבע אמות, which should acquire it for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? When it falls, it falls within her own ארבע אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. Even if her hand did not acquire the גט, her ארבע אמות should.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area of four אמות around a person can acquire an object for her. A גט sliding off her hand should drop into that area, so she should be divorced that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The four-cubit area around a person, which can acquire things for her

phrases.english: Why?
But when it falls
it falls within her four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's ruling in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that she is not divorced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her ארבע אמות acquire for her, and the גט falls into them, so she should be divorced.

steps.title: The גט did not rest in her area
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the גט rolled away and did not come to rest within her ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it did not come to rest there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing רב יהודה's case. The גט kept going and did not settle inside her ארבע אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her ארבע אמות only acquire an object that actually lands and stays there. If it bounced or rolled beyond, they never acquired it.

phrases.english: Where it did not come to rest there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט lands in her ארבע אמות, so she should be divorced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט never rested in her ארבע אמות, so they did not acquire it.

steps.title: Let the air of her four אמות acquire it
steps.stepSummary: Even if it did not rest there, the גט passed through the airspace of her ארבע אמות. Why doesn't that divorce her?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her be divorced through the airspace of the ארבע אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. While flying, the גט was in the air above her ארבע אמות, so maybe that should count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the airspace above her ארבע אמות counts as part of them, then the גט was in her area the moment it passed through. Where it finally landed would not matter.

phrases.english: But let her be divorced
from the airspace of the four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the גט did not rest in her ארבע אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without resting, the גט passed through the air of her ארבע אמות, which might acquire it.

steps.title: Then this would settle רבי אלעזר's question
steps.stepSummary: If she is not divorced, רב יהודה's ruling would show that ארבע אמות do not include their airspace. That would answer רבי אלעזר's open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then resolve what רבי אלעזר asked: the ארבע אמות the חכמים spoke of, do they have airspace or not? Resolve that they do not have airspace!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב יהודה's ruling. If the airspace does not divorce her, then רבי אלעזר's unanswered question is now settled: ארבע אמות do not include airspace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר asked whether ארבע אמות acquire an object while it is in the air above them, and he left the question open. רב יהודה rules that she is not divorced even though the גט flew over her area. That would seem to prove the airspace does not count.

phrases.english: Then resolve what Rabbi Elazar asked:
The four cubits that the Sages spoke of,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהֶן אֲוִיר אוֹ אֵין לָהֶן אֲוִיר?
phrases.english: do they have airspace or do they not have airspace?
Resolve that they do not have airspace!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 27: either she should be divorced, or רבי אלעזר's question is settled.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's question whether ארבע אמות include their airspace
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ruling that the גט flying over her area does not divorce her

steps.title: The case is a woman standing by a river
steps.stepSummary: No proof: רב יהודה's case is a woman at a riverbank. The גט is headed to be lost in the water from the start, so even the air of her ארבע אמות would not acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A woman standing at the riverbank, where from the start the גט stands to be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof. It explains that רב יהודה's case is a special situation, so it tells us nothing about רבי אלעזר's general question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a riverbank, a גט that slides off her hand will fall into the water and be lost. An object on its way to destruction is not acquired even through the airspace. So רבי אלעזר's question stays open for normal cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Stands to be lost or destroyed

steps.whatToRemember: A גט only divorces if it truly comes into her possession: her hand must be able to hold it, or it must rest in her ארבע אמות. רב יהודה's case does not settle whether airspace counts, because a גט falling toward a river is lost from the outset.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not decide here whether ארבע אמות include airspace. It only shows that רב יהודה's case cannot prove the answer.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With a woman standing at the riverbank,
where from the start it stands to be lost.
phrases.notes: If the גט slides off her hand, it drops into the river, so it was never really going to reach her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 28 by limiting רב יהודה's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof about airspace. רב יהודה's ruling itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יהודה's case is a גט headed to be lost in a river, which even airspace would not acquire, so it proves nothing about normal cases.
